explanation: Pointing a single index finger directly at a person in Thailand is seen as rude and accusatory, so Thais more often indicate a person by tilting their chin in that direction. Pointing at inanimate objects or animals is generally tolerated, though using the whole hand rather than one finger is considered more polite either way.
local_tip: If you need to indicate a person, tilt your chin toward them instead of pointing; for objects, an open hand is more polite than a single finger.

also_check.note: Pointing with the index finger is considered impolite; an open hand is used instead.
Pointing is generally acceptable in casual settings, though it can seem blunt in formal ones.
